video_title: How Stephon Castle is SETTING THE TONE with his PHYSICALITY in the Finals 👏 | NBA Today

quotes.speaker: Stephon Castle
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Castle on his aggressive approach in Game 3
quotes.excerpt: I feel like I was pretty close to getting there, especially in the first half.

text_blocks.speaker: Malika Andrews
text_blocks.text: You said that when you get to your spots, there's not really anybody that can guard you. How close were you to that zone in Game 3?

text_blocks.speaker: Stephon Castle
text_blocks.text: I feel like I was pretty close to getting there, especially in the first half. I was very decisive and when I wanted to drive, I made it a point that I wanted to get to my spot and finish. I think it set the tone for the rest of the game, just being able to touch paint.

quotes.speaker: Stephon Castle
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Castle on the Spurs' confidence to win the series
quotes.excerpt: I expect us to win the next three.

text_blocks.speaker: Malika Andrews
text_blocks.text: Do you walk into Madison Square Garden expecting to win Game 4?

text_blocks.speaker: Stephon Castle
text_blocks.text: Yeah, definitely. I expect us to win the next three. We are just taking it game by game, quarter by quarter, and trying to walk this thing down. Those first two games really hurt and I feel like it was an eye-opener for us, but with the group that we have and what we've shown all year, I don't got nothing but confidence in them.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins praises Stephon Castle's physicality and impact
quotes.excerpt: I love the confidence but I also love the physicality of Stephon Castle on both ends.

text_blocks.speaker: Malika Andrews
text_blocks.text: You got to love the confidence from a 21-year-old kid.

text_blocks.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
text_blocks.text: What else is he supposed to say? They going to lose? Nah, I love the confidence but I also love the physicality of Stephon Castle on both ends of the floor. And I know Wembanyama got a lot of flowers and praise for what he done, but Stephon Castle set the tone.

quotes.speaker: Jeremy Lin
quotes.summary_phrase: Jeremy Lin highlights Stephon Castle's poise and decision-making
quotes.excerpt: It's the two turnovers to me. That is something where his playmaking ability is improving.
quotes.quote: Stephon Castle is growing up right before our eyes. It's the two turnovers to me. That is something where his playmaking ability, his ability to take care of the ball, his decision-making, every game he is improving. His ability to be poised and to not get into tight spaces, to not have these pick-six turnovers where they get an easy two, these are all part of his development and his growth.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins on Stephon Castle's solid foundation and footwork
quotes.excerpt: He has such a solid foundation with his lower that he can take it as slow as he wants.
quotes.quote: He has such a solid foundation with his lower that he can take it as slow as he wants, but it throws people off. I don't know how he gets the ball up sometimes when he does it, but all I can tell y'all is that he got some of the best brakes that I've seen in this league.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins on the Spurs' three-guard lineup adjustment
quotes.excerpt: They went with that three-guard lineup and what happened was it took pressure off of Castle.
quotes.quote: They went with that three-guard lineup and what happened was it took pressure off of Castle. That's what I'm saying about overthinking. You could tell that the conversation with Castle was, we don't need you to be the point guard, we need you to be aggressive. And he was going to get his.

quotes.speaker: Zach Lowe
quotes.summary_phrase: Zach Lowe explains the Spurs' defensive strategy against Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: They essentially went to a zone. Their whole point was, can we keep Wembanyama in the paint?
quotes.quote: They essentially went to a zone. Their whole point was, can we keep Wembanyama in the paint? And if he's guarding the paint, he switches over, gets swung around, and this is what they're okay with. They are okay with him closing out to the corner. They do not want him above the free-throw line on the wing or top of the key.
